# Screenrecord patch to windows-capture 2.0.1

Source: crates.io package `windows-capture` 2.0.1, copied from the locked Cargo registry source. The original MIT licence remains in `LICENCE`.

The encoder's two unbounded channels use `SyncSender` with capacity two. Constructors and replacement channels in finalization use the same helper. Submission documentation now describes backpressure. The regression test checks full-queue behavior, ordered delivery, and end-of-stream delivery.

Screenrecord disables this dependency's audio encoder and records audio separately with WASAPI. Combined audio/video submission has not been validated with this patch. The limit covers queued payloads. The producer, consumer, retained capture frame, and native encoder also hold memory. A native encoder that remains alive but unresponsive can still block finalization. Screenrecord's cleanup registry bounds caller waiting and prevents recovery from racing outstanding writers while native threads are running.

Run `cargo test --manifest-path vendor/windows-capture/Cargo.toml --lib bounded_queue_tests --locked --target-dir target` from the Screenrecord workspace. Physical capture throughput, frame drops, and driver behavior remain device-test requirements.

Version 0.4.1 uses `Direct3D11CaptureFramePool::CreateFreeThreaded` with two frame buffers so frame arrival does not require dispatcher delivery. Frame-pool HRESULT failures now stop the worker and propagate through its join result. Capture closes before dispatcher shutdown. A failed WM_QUIT post retains and joins the native worker instead of detaching it; the app's cleanup registry bounds caller waiting while keeping ownership.

Video submission now copies both same-size and resized WGC surfaces into separate owned textures on the capture context, flushes the copy, and queues only the owned surface. The prior same-size path retained a pool surface after returning its capture frame, and the resized path overwrote a shared cached surface while the transcoder could still use it. The two-payload queue remains bounded; one producer copy and media-pipeline allocations are additional. Copies are not reused while the asynchronous media pipeline can reference them. Screenrecord's callback mutex serializes capture and static-frame use of the immediate context. New texture allocation/copy throughput and physical multi-monitor behavior require manual validation.

Payload submission checks the owned transcoder thread every 2 ms while the two-item queue is full. Both initial and later `TranscodeAsync` failures, unexpected completion, and panics become errors after joining the completed worker. Finish and Drop close both channels before joining; receivers drain queued payloads before disconnect signals EOS. They no longer try to enqueue an EOS sentinel into a full queue whose consumer has failed.

Seven source-free tests run with `cargo test --manifest-path vendor/windows-capture/Cargo.toml --lib --locked --target-dir target`: queue backpressure, late video/audio consumer failure, full-queue drain, completed/panicked consumers, an MTA thread without a dispatcher creating/closing a free-threaded WARP frame pool, immutable WARP surface pixels after source overwrite with crop/pad dimensions, and failed-stop ownership. No capture item or session is created by these tests. This is a plausible delivery fix for the observed startup timeout, not a claim that a physical monitor retry has succeeded.

`cargo test -p screenrecord-capture media_contract_native_encoder_finish_and_drop_drain_every_queued_frame --locked -- --ignored --nocapture` also runs the actual Windows encoder against synthetic BGRA frames in an owned child with a 30-second deadline. Finish and Drop each preserve all 12 frames; bundled FFmpeg decodes the files and verifies the final color. Set `SCREENRECORD_FFMPEG` to the bundled executable first. Logs are `artifacts/audit-0.4.1/vendor-capture-tests.log` and `artifacts/audit-0.4.1/native-encoder-drain.log`.

Primary contracts: [CreateFreeThreaded](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/uwp/api/windows.graphics.capture.direct3d11captureframepool.createfreethreaded), [capture frame and surface lifetime](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/develop/media-authoring-processing/screen-capture), and [D3D11 immediate-context synchronization](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/direct3d11/overviews-direct3d-11-render-multi-thread-intro).

Version 0.4.3 removes the unused DispatcherQueueController from the dedicated free-threaded capture worker. Early initialization errors previously bypassed its required asynchronous shutdown. A plain Win32 queue is created with PeekMessage(PM_NOREMOVE) before StartCapture; the existing WM_QUIT loop and owned join remain. The synchronous `start` API is unchanged and is not used by Screenrecord. Microsoft documents both the [current-thread dispatcher shutdown requirement](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/dispatcherqueue/nf-dispatcherqueue-createdispatcherqueuecontroller) and [message-queue creation before PostThreadMessage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winuser/nf-winuser-postthreadmessagew).

Construction now has an armed rollback guard from frame-pool creation until ownership transfers to GraphicsCaptureApi. Every later failure revokes registered handlers and closes the session before the pool. Previously a failed session setter could strand the FrameArrived closure's strong reference to its own pool. Normal teardown uses the same session-before-pool order as the [Windows capture sample](https://github.com/robmikh/Win32CaptureSample/blob/master/Win32CaptureSample/SimpleCapture.cpp).

Atomic diagnostics distinguish native startup, FrameArrived entry, frame acquisition, content size, resize, surface/texture conversion, callback-lock waiting, and application-handler delivery. Event counts and HRESULTs do not contain captured content. Three added source-free tests verify these checkpoints, an early WM_QUIT surviving message-queue initialization, and real WARP pool event registration rollback releasing a strong reference cycle. The latter registers an event without creating a capture item or session. These fixes and diagnostics do not prove the cause of the two intermittent 0.4.2 first-frame failures or successful physical capture afterward.

Both video encoder constructors now initialize WinRT on the transcoder worker before taking its prepared transcode result and transcoder. An initialization error leaves those objects owned by the parent encoder for cleanup on its initialized thread. Two tests exercise actual MediaTranscoder methods/destruction in the worker and injected initialization failure with retained parent ownership. Twelve vendor tests pass. The bounded native encode regression also covers file and in-memory stream constructors, each finalized by Finish and Drop, verifying all 12 frames and final colors through complete decode. Logs: `artifacts/audit-0.4.3/vendor-capture-tests.log` and `artifacts/audit-0.4.3/native-encoder-drain.log`. This follows Microsoft's [per-thread RoInitialize contract](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/roapi/nf-roapi-roinitialize).

## First-frame sizing and bounded encoder submission in 0.7.4

Frame arrival uses the dimensions passed to `CreateFreeThreaded`. Reading the capture item's size again after allocating the pool could discard an otherwise valid first frame during a display or window resize. The callback skips transient nonpositive content dimensions and records the `empty_content` diagnostic stage. Only a positive size change recreates the pool.

Video and audio submission preserve queued samples and report an error if the live Windows transcoder leaves its queue full for ten seconds. Native shutdown still retains ownership through the existing cleanup worker when a driver call remains blocked.
